lines.kr: Bonjou! Ça va?
lines.en: Hello! How’s it going?

lines.kr: Ç’apé kouri, mærsi. É twa? Komen to yê?
lines.en: It’s going, thanks. And you? How are you?

lines.kr: Mo byin, mærsi. Ki çé tô nom?
lines.en: I’m good, thanks. What’s your name?

lines.kr: Yé pèl mò Joseph. É twa?
lines.en: They call me Joseph. And you?

lines.kr: Mô nom çé Max.
lines.en: My name is Max.

lines.kr: Mo konten fé lakònésans avèk twa.
lines.en: I’m happy to meet you.

lines.kr: Paréy. Orévwar!
lines.en: Same. Goodbye!

lines.kr: Orévwar, twa!
lines.en: Goodbye!

lines.kr: Hé, Louis! Komen lê zafær?
lines.en: Hey, Louis! How are things?

lines.kr: Konm-çi-konm-ça, mèsi.
lines.en: OK, thanks.

lines.kr: To gin ti-nom?
lines.en: Do you have a nickname?

lines.kr: Wi, mo ti-nom çé Lou.
lines.en: Yes, my nickname is Lou.

lines.kr: Vayan! Mo pa gin ti-nom, mò.
lines.en: Awesome! I don’t have a nickname, me.

lines.kr: Domaj.
lines.en: Too bad.

title: Where are you from? What do you do?

lines.kr: Éyou to sòr?
lines.en: Where are you from?

lines.kr: Mo sòr o Shikago. É twa?
lines.en: I’m from Chicago. And you?

lines.kr: Mo sòr o Zopélousas.
lines.en: I’m from Opelousas.

lines.kr: Ki to fé pou louvraj?
lines.en: What do you do for work?

lines.kr: Mo çé moun lwil. Mo travay dan klo lwil.
lines.en: I work in the oil industry. I work in the oilfield.

lines.kr: Mò, mo çé mèt-lékol o Nouvèl-Òrléan.
lines.en: Me, I’m a teacher in New Orleans.

title: Where are you from? What do you do?

lines.kr: Ki çé tô louvraj?
lines.en: What’s your job?

lines.kr: Mo pa gin djòb astœr, la.
lines.en: I don’t have a job right now.

lines.kr: T’apé sharshé pou kishòj?
lines.en: Are you looking for something?

lines.kr: Sûr! M’olé travayé konm labitan.
lines.en: Sure! I want to work as a farmer.

lines.kr: Çé dur, do, padna.
lines.en: It’s hard, though, friend.

lines.kr: Kòfær?
lines.en: Why?

lines.kr: Parske çé livær — na pli louvraj jiska printem-la.
lines.en: Because it’s winter — there is no more work until the spring.

lines.kr: Shak!
lines.en: Shucks!

title: When is your birthday? How old are you?

lines.kr: Bon fèt, Paul! Kombyin zan to fé?
lines.en: Happy birthday, Paul! How old are you turning?

lines.kr: Mo fé kinz zan. Kèl laj to gin, Nonk Jim?
lines.en: I’m turning fifteen. How old are you, Uncle Jim?

lines.kr: Mo pli vyé ke twa; mo gin swasant zan.
lines.en: I’m older than you; I’m sixty years old.

lines.kr: To byin vyé! Mo pli jœn ke twa. Kèl jour tô fèt?
lines.en: You’re real old! I’m younger than you. What day is your birthday?

lines.kr: Mô fèt çé vint-wit mars.
lines.en: My birthday is the 28th of March.

lines.kr: M’a fé twa in gato pou tô fèt, Nonk Jim!
lines.en: I’m going to make a cake for your birthday, Uncle Jim!

title: When is your birthday? How old are you?

lines.kr: Moman, dan ki lanné to té né?
lines.en: Mom, what year were you born?

lines.kr: Mo té né dan mil-nèf-sen-sinkant.
lines.en: I was born in 1950.

lines.kr: Dan ki mwa?
lines.en: In what month?

lines.kr: Dan mwa avril.
lines.en: In the month of April.

lines.kr: Épi ki jour?
lines.en: And what day?

lines.kr: Sèt-la.
lines.en: The 7th.

lines.kr: Alòr, tô fèt çé sèt avril-la?
lines.en: So, your birthday is the 7th of April?

lines.kr: Wé, é bliy pa ça!
lines.en: Yes, and don’t forget it!

lines.kr: Ki moun nonm-çála?
lines.en: Who’s that man?

lines.kr: Li çé mô frær.
lines.en: That’s my brother.

lines.kr: Kwa çé sô nom?
lines.en: What’s his name?

lines.kr: Sô nom çé Robert, mé sô ti-nom çé Ti-Rob.
lines.en: His name is Robert, but is nickname is Ti-Rob.

lines.kr: Kombyin frær to gin?
lines.en: How many brothers do you have?

lines.kr: Mo gin ènn frær é dé sœr. Mô frær-yé pi résté isit.
lines.en: I have one brother and two sisters. My brothers don’t live here anymore.

lines.kr: Ça-fé, fenm-la çé tô sœr?
lines.en: So, that woman is your sister?

lines.kr: Non, çé mô kouzinn.
lines.en: No, that’s my cousin.

lines.kr: Kombyin moun yé gin dan tô famiy?
lines.en: How many people do you have in your family?

lines.kr: Ina sink moun: mò, mô pær, mô nonk, mô tant, é mô kouzin.
lines.en: There are five people: me, my father, my uncle, my aunt and my cousin.

lines.kr: É tô mær?
lines.en: And your mother?

lines.kr: Mô moman mouri trò zan pasé.
lines.en: My mother died three years ago.

lines.kr: Ô, mo shagrin.
lines.en: Oh, I’m sorry.

lines.kr: Mærsi; mò osit.
lines.en: Thank you; me too.

lines.kr: Kombyin shanm ina dan tô lamézon?
lines.en: How many rooms are there in your house?

lines.kr: Ina lakizinn, dé shanm-a-koushé, salon-la, é ina ènn shanm-a-bin. Ça fé yé gin sink shanm. É tô-chin?
lines.en: There is the kitchen, two bedrooms, the living room, and a bathroom. So, they have six rooms. And yours?

lines.kr: Mô-chin gin sèt shanm: lakizinn, dé shanm-a-bin, dé shanm-a-koushé, salon-la é in lakav.
lines.en: My house has seven rooms: the kitchen, two bathrooms, two bedrooms, the living room and a basement.

lines.kr: Tô lakav enba?
lines.en: Is your basement underneath?

lines.kr: Wi.
lines.en: Yes.

lines.kr: No pe pa gin lakav enba o Nouvèl-Òrléan. Ina tro dolo. To gin lashans, twa.
lines.en: We can’t have basements underneath in New Orleans. There’s too much water. You’re lucky, you.

lines.kr: Petèt, mé vouzòt rès dan Lalwizyann é mo rès dan Indiana. Ça fé vouzòt gin lashans!
lines.en: Maybe, but y’all live in Louisiana and I live in Indiana. Y’all are lucky!

lines.kr: Hm. To gin rézon, la.
lines.en: Hm. You’re right about that.

lines.kr: Mo bézwin komod-la! Éyou li yê?
lines.en: I need the toilet! Where is it?

lines.kr: Li enho lèskalyé. Dèzyèm zétaj-la.
lines.en: It’s up the stairs. The second floor.

lines.kr: OK, mærsi!
lines.en: OK, thanks!

lines.kr: Pa-d-kwa.
lines.en: You’re welcome.

lines.kr: Byin, byin mærsi; mo mank èksplozé!
lines.en: Thanks so much; I’m almost exploding!

lines.kr: Çé pa aryin, mé fé vit, la! Ç’alé sòrti salé si to fé pipi sur planshé mô gran-mær.
lines.en: It’s nothing, but be quick! It’s going to end up badly if you pee on my grandmother’s floor.

lines.kr: Komen tem-la jòrdi?
lines.en: How is the weather?

lines.kr: Li mòyær kouvær; ina bokou nwaj.
lines.en: It’s quite cloudy; there’s a lot of clouds.

lines.kr: Li fé fré?
lines.en: Is it cold?

lines.kr: Non, li fé bo. T’olé kouri o park?
lines.en: No, the weather is good. Do you want to go to the park?

lines.kr: Petèt. Ça senm lapli?
lines.en: Maybe. Does it seem like it will rain?

lines.kr: Mo pa konné, mé mo krò pa. To pens t’a fonn si to mouyé?
lines.en: I don’t know, I don’t think so. Do you think you’ll melt if you’re wet?

lines.kr: Non, shær, mé mo p’olé barbouyé mô nouvo bòt-yé!
lines.en: No, cher, but I don’t want to get my new boots dirty!

lines.kr: Byin, kòfær to ashté bòt si yé pe pa marshé dan labou?
lines.en: Well, why did you buy the boots if they can’t walk in mud?

lines.kr: Ki kalité plant yé gin dan lakour?
lines.en: What kind of plants do they have in the courtyard?

lines.kr: Tou kalité. Ina dê narb, dê flœr, dê zærb, tou kishòj.
lines.en: All kinds. There are trees, flowers, grass, everything.

lines.kr: Moun ka manjé ça?
lines.en: Can people eat that?

lines.kr: Zen dê plant to ka manjé; no sær féy sasafra pou fé lapoud filé é no mèt ça dan gombo. Li gou bon!
lines.en: There are plants you can eat; we use sassafras leaves to make filé powder and we put it in gumbo. It tastes good!

lines.kr: Kèl lœr vouzòt kour lékòl?
lines.en: What time do y’all go to school?

lines.kr: No kour lékòl a wit œr shak matin.
lines.en: We go to school at eight o’clock every morning.

lines.kr: Çé bonnœr! Mo té konné kouri lékòl a nèf œr. É kan zòt vyin bæk lamézon?
lines.en: That’s early! I used to go to school at nine o’clock. And when do you come home?

lines.kr: No kit lékòl a trò zœr, no èspær bòs-la, é no vyin bæk lamézon a trò zœr é demi.
lines.en: We leave school at three o’clock, we wait for the bus, and we come back home at half past three.

lines.kr: Ki jour to fé tô ménaj?
lines.en: What day do you do your chores?

lines.kr: En jénéral mo fé mô ménaj pendan fin-lasmènn. É twa?
lines.en: In general I do my chores on the weekend. And you?

lines.kr: Çé byin rar mo fé mô-chin ménaj. Mo mand mô bèl pou fé li.
lines.en: I hardly ever do my own chores. I ask my girlfriend to do it.

lines.kr: Vilin! Kòfær to fé ça?
lines.en: That’s mean! Why do you do that?

lines.kr: Mé mo travay pendan tou lasmènn!
lines.en: But I work all week!

lines.kr: É li-mèm?
lines.en: And her?

lines.kr: Wé… li travay osit…
lines.en: Yeah… She works too...

lines.kr: Alòr senm to gin pou édé li èk ménaj-la.
lines.en: Well it seems like you have to help her out with the chores.

lines.kr: John, ça to linm fé kan to travay pa?
lines.en: John, what do you like to do when you don’t work?

lines.kr: Mo linm bwa labyær é asit prenn lafrèsh enn lagalri.
lines.en: I like to drink beer and take the air on the porch.

lines.kr: Ça senm bon. To kout lamizik?
lines.en: That sounds good. Do you listen to music?

lines.kr: Wi, mo linm ça osit. Zen dê fwa mo kout lamizik tandi m’apé asit ònn lagalri.
lines.en: Yes, I like that too. Sometimes I listen to music while I’m sitting on the porch.

lines.kr: Mo linm péshé kan mo gin tem.
lines.en: I like to fish when I have time.

lines.kr: Ki kalité pwason to linm trapé?
lines.en: What kind of fish do you like to catch?

lines.kr: Mo linm trapé dê patasa parske yé gou bon. Mo linm pa tro pwason-armin, la.
lines.en: I like to catch sunfish because they taste good. I don’t like gar too much.

lines.kr: Proshin fwa to trap in pwason-armin, mènn mò ça!
lines.en: Next time you catch a gar, bring it to me!

lines.kr: OK, mô fiy, ça t’olé fé? T’olé monté bisik?
lines.en: OK, my girl, what do you want to do? Do you want to ride your bike?

lines.kr: Non!
lines.en: No!

lines.kr: T’olé kouri najé?
lines.en: Do you want to go swimming?

lines.kr: Non!
lines.en: No!

lines.kr: Alòr, ça ina èk twa?
lines.en: So what’s up with you?

lines.kr: To promèt pou ménné mò gété “The Princess and the Frog”! To fé særmen!
lines.en: You promised to take me to watch “The Princess and the Frog”! You swore you would!

lines.kr: Ki ça to mèt kan li fé fré déyòr?
lines.en: What do you wear when it’s cold outside?

lines.kr: Mo mèt shapo, jakèt, kilot, èk in pær bòt.
lines.en: I wear a hat, jacket, pants and a pair of boots.

lines.kr: Ékan tem-la bo?
lines.en: And when the weather is nice?

lines.kr: Lá, mo ot tou ça é mo mèt mô kilot kout, in T-shirt, é mô sandal-yé.
lines.en: Then, I take all that off and put on short pants, a t-shirt, and my sandals.

lines.kr: Mo linm pa pòrté sandal akòz mô pyé-yé vini barbouyé.
lines.en: I don’t like to wear sandals because my feet get dirty.

lines.kr: Alòr, marsh pa dan labou, padna.
lines.en: Well then don’t walk in the mud, friend.

lines.kr: To gin in joli lajup la! Mo linm koulœr-la.
lines.en: You have a pretty skirt there! I love the color.

lines.kr: Mærsi! Mo linm koulœr tô ròb la osit.
lines.en: Thanks! I love the color of your dress too.

lines.kr: T’olé mo édé twa oté tô jakèt?
lines.en: Do you want me to help you take your jacket off?

lines.kr: O, byin mærsi, mô fiy. Éyou tô-chin jakèt?
lines.en: Oh, thanks a lot, my girl. Where’s your own jacket?

lines.kr: Mo pa pòrté jakèt jòrdi, moman.
lines.en: I wasn’t wearing a jacket today, mom.

lines.kr: To va trapé in larimm!
lines.en: You’re going to catch a cold!

lines.kr: Ça ina?
lines.en: What’s up?

lines.kr: Mo sen pa mò tro byin.
lines.en: I don’t feel too good.

lines.kr: Ki çé ça ki fé mal?
lines.en: What’s hurting?

lines.kr: Mô lèstoma fé mal; mo gin mal-lèstoma.
lines.en: My stomach hurts; I have a stomach ache.

lines.kr: Ki ça to manjé yær?
lines.en: What did you eat yesterday?

lines.kr: Mo pa konné… enlentour kinz liv krévis?
lines.en: I don’t know… around fifteen pounds of crawfish?

lines.kr: Senm to malad ojòrdi!
lines.en: It seems you’re sick today!

lines.kr: Wi, mo t’apé tousé épi étærné dépi bonnœr matin-çila.
lines.en: Yes, I’ve been coughing and sneezing since early this morning.

lines.kr: Prenn latizann avèk dimyèl. Ça va èdé twa.
lines.en: Take herbal tea with milk. That will help you.

lines.kr: Mærsi, m’a fé ça talœr.
lines.en: Thanks, I’ll do that later.

lines.kr: Mèt kèk féy dibonm endan li.
lines.en: Put some mint leaves in it.

lines.kr: OK, mo gin dité kammòmèl shé mò.
lines.en: OK, I have some chamomile tea at my place.

lines.kr: Hé! Vyin gété in pòrtré avèk nouzòt aswa.
lines.en: Hey! Come watch a movie with us tonight.

lines.kr: Mo sé linmé, mé mô tèt fé mal.
lines.en: I’d love to, but my head hurts.

lines.kr: Kòfær to jamé olé sòrti èk nou?
lines.en: Why do you never want to come out with us?

lines.kr: Mo pe pa gété pòrtré kan mo gin in tèl mal-latèt.
lines.en: I can’t watch a movie when I have a headache.

lines.kr: Gin lè to linm pa gin bon tem.
lines.en: Seems like you don’t like to have a good time.

lines.kr: Çé pa ça, mo jish sen mò ti brin malad. In nòt fwa, zanmi.
lines.en: It’s not that, I just feel a little sick. Another time, friend.

lines.kr: Bonswa, boug! No va fé sosyété démin oswa. T’olé vini?
lines.en: Good evening, dude! We’re going to throw a party tomorrow evening. Do you want to come?

lines.kr: Ki lœr?
lines.en: What time?

lines.kr: Ora wit lœr.
lines.en: Around eight o’clock.

lines.kr: Éyou?
lines.en: Where?

lines.kr: Lamézon mô paren-yé. Yé gin bokou plas pou toukèkènn.
lines.en: My parents’ house. They have a lot of space for everyone.

lines.kr: Dakòr, mo va dèt la. Mærsi!
lines.en: OK, I’ll be there. Thanks!

lines.kr: Éyou t’apé kouri?
lines.en: Where are you going?

lines.kr: M’ap kouri a lagrosri, mé mo pærdi.
lines.en: I’m going to the grocery store, but I’m lost.

lines.kr: Pou arivé a lagrosri, kontini dé mil épi tòrn a gosh kan to wa gro sipré-la. Swiv shmin- çála jiska lagrosri la. Di Misyé Charlot bonjou pou sô zanmi Freddy.
lines.en: To get to the grocery store, continue two miles and then turn left when you see the big cedar. Follow that road until the grocery store. Tell Mister Charlot hello from his friend Freddy.

lines.kr: Byin mærsi!
lines.en: Thanks a lot!

lines.kr: Ki ça vouzòt apé fé pendan lété?
lines.en: What are you going to do during the summer?

lines.kr: No va rodayé jiska Kanada.
lines.en: We’re going to take a road trip to Canada.

lines.kr: Ça yé gin laba?
lines.en: What do they have over there?

lines.kr: Yé gin in ta pou wa é fé. Lavil Montréal gin in gro fèt lamizik djaz, ina bokou park nasyonal, é toukishòj.
lines.en: They have a lot to see and do. The city of Montreal has a big jazz music festival, there are a lot of national parks, and everything.

lines.kr: Mé tem-la fé fré laba, wi?
lines.en: But the weather is cold over there, yeah?

lines.kr: Pa dan lété. Li byin bo.
lines.en: Not in the summer. It’s really nice.

lines.kr: Alòr kombyin jour vou bézwin pou kouri la?
lines.en: So how many days do y’all need to get there?

lines.kr: N’a prenn trò kat jour.
lines.en: We’re taking three or four days.

lines.kr: Yéyay, mo gin in ta pou fé démin! Mo gin pou kouri a Lafayèt pou ashté kèk nouvo linj pou mô piti. Apré ça, m'ap kouri wa mô bèl-sœr a Sésilya. Apré ça, mo stil gin pou fé grosri...
lines.en: Yeyay, I have a ton to do tomorrow! I have to go to Lafayette to buy some new clothes for my children. After that, I’m going to see my sister-in-law in Cecilia. After that, I still have to go make groceries…

lines.kr: Mé mò, mo gin pou kouri o sto démin itou. Si to di mò ça to bezwin, m'alé ashté kèk zafær pou twa.
lines.en: But me, I have to go to the store tomorrow too. If you tell me what you need, I’ll buy some things for you.

lines.kr: Mé ça çé vayan, shær! Gèt, ça çé mô lis. Si to ashèt tou ça, mo sa bokou konten!
lines.en: But that’s real nice of you! Look, this is my list. If you buy all that, I’ll be really happy!

lines.kr: Oké, alon wa... mé, shær, to ékri in ta zafær isit!
lines.en: OK, let’s see… but, cher, you wrote a whole bunch of stuff here!

lines.kr: Wèl, si mo ashèt pa in ta, no va pa gin asé pou manjé. Çé lafèt mô garçon é tou la famiy vyin manjé shé nouzòt!
lines.en: Well, if I don’t buy a whole bunch, we won’t have enough to eat. It’s my son’s birthday and all the family are coming to our place!

lines.kr: Si mo té konné ça, mo sé pa di ariyin!
lines.en: If I had known that, I wouldn’t have said anything!

lines.kr: Ça to sé fé si to sé ganñé lalotri?
lines.en: What would you do if you won the lottery?

lines.kr: Mò, mo sé kité mô djòb, bati mò in nouvo mézon dan la kamponñ, épi résté la tousœl.
lines.en: Me, I’d leave my job, build myself a new house in the country, and live alone.

lines.kr: Mé si to rès laba tousœl, to sa ennwiyé!
lines.en: But if you live there alone, you’ll be bored!

lines.kr: Mo p'olé pærsonn vini embarasé mò pou mô larjen. Ça fé mo sé kouri résté obòr bayou laba la éyou mô ti frèr fé lashas.
lines.en: I don’t want anyone to come and bother me for my money. So I’d go and live by the bayou there where my little brother goes hunting.

lines.kr: Laba, lá? Wé, mo konné! Si to ganñ lalotri é to gonn laba, m'a vini vizité!
lines.en: Down there? Yeah, I know! If you win the lottery and you go down there, I’ll come visit!

lines.kr: Mé to kanay, twa!
lines.en: You’re sly, you!

lines.kr: Ki ça k’apé dansé avèk Marie, lá?
lines.en: Who’s that dancing with Marie, there?

lines.kr: Çé mô kouzin, Billy. Senm l’ap fé lakour apré ti fiy-çála.
lines.en: That’s my cousin, Billy. Seems like he’s dating that girl there.

lines.kr: Yé pe dansé bokou byin!
lines.en: They can dance really well!

lines.kr: Lamizik isit çé vayan aswa, la.
lines.en: The music here is awesome tonight.

lines.kr: Kèk moun légliz va fé sosyété pou fèt mô moman. T’olé vini èk mò?
lines.en: Some people from church are going to throw a party for my mother’s birthday. Do you want to come with me?

lines.kr: Yé va gin lamizik?
lines.en: Will they have music?

lines.kr: O, wi! Nora lamizik, manjé, divin, tou ça.
lines.en: Oh, yes! There will be music, food, wine, all that.

lines.kr: No va dansé ensenm?
lines.en: Are we going to dance together?

lines.kr: Si t’olé, shær!
lines.en: If you want, cher!

lines.kr: Mo jamé kouri in fèt san dansé.
lines.en: I never go to a party without dancing.

lines.kr: Ça yé konné fé pendan in laboushri?
lines.en: What do they usually do during a boucherie?

lines.kr: Yé chou kèk koshon, é yé fé toukishòj avèk li. Boudin, landoui, toukishòj kom ça.
lines.en: They kill some pigs, and they’d make all kinds of stuff with it. Boudin, andouille, all kinds of stuff like that.

lines.kr: Çé tou?
lines.en: That’s all?

lines.kr: Wi, é tem-zen-tem ina lamizik.
lines.en: Yes, and sometimes there’s music.

lines.kr: Yé chou bèf osit?
lines.en: Do they kill cattle too?

lines.kr: Wi, mé pa en minm tem.
lines.en: Yes, but not at the same time.

lines.kr: Mô gran-mær planté sô jardin yær matin.
lines.en: My grandma planted her garden yesterday morning.

lines.kr: Kwa li planté?
lines.en: What did she plant?

lines.kr: Li planté ti margo patat anglèz, patat dous, zònyon, tomat, mayi taktak…
lines.en: She planted starters for English potatoes, sweet potatoes, onions, tomatoes, popcorn…

lines.kr: Mo linm taktak! Ékan li va dèt paré?
lines.en: I love popcorn! When will it be ready?

lines.kr: Ifo spéré, padna. Ça ka prenn kèk mwa.
lines.en: You have to wait, buddy. We have to wait a few months.

lines.kr: Kèk mwa? Non. M’ap kouri lagrosri ashté mô-chin taktak, mærsi bokou.
lines.en: A few months? No. I’m going to the grocery store and buying my own popcorn, thank you very much.

lines.kr: To linm tô manjé byin sézonné?
lines.en: Do you like your food well seasoned?

lines.kr: Wé, mèt bokou pimen é zépis endan li.
lines.en: Yes, put a lot of pepper and spice in there.

lines.kr: To jamé manjé dan Lalwizyann.
lines.en: You’ve never eaten in Louisiana.

lines.kr: Non, kòfær?
lines.en: No, why?

lines.kr: Ariyin. Vwala tô gombo.
lines.en: Nothing. Here’s your gumbo.

lines.kr: KO! Çé difé la!
lines.en: KO! It’s fire!

lines.kr: Mo séyé di twa…
lines.en: I tried to tell you…

lines.kr: Dolo! Vit!
lines.en: Water! Quick!

lines.kr: Komen to kwi lê zariko?
lines.en: How do you cook your green beans?

lines.kr: Mo mèt yé dan dolo aswa avan m’olé kwi yé. Lá, mo fé yé bouyi épi konsommé pendan kèk lœr.
lines.en: I put them in water the evening before I cook them. Then I boil them and then eat them within a few hours.

lines.kr: To mèt ça avèk diri?
lines.en: Do you put them with rice?

lines.kr: Wé! To pe pa manjé zariko san diri.
lines.en: Yes! You can’t eat beans without rice.

lines.kr: Jòrdi çé Karnaval!
lines.en: Today is Carnival!

lines.kr: Wé! N’a gin in bon tem pou Mardi Gra-la!
lines.en: Yes! We’re going to have a good time for Mardi Gras!

lines.kr: Démin çé Mærkrédi dê Senn é Karèm-la komens.
lines.en: Tomorrow is Ash Wednesday and Lent begins.

lines.kr: La, no va fé mèg jiska Jour Pak-la.
lines.en: Then, we’re going to fast until Easter Day.

lines.kr: Misyé, misyé! Garòsh mò dê biy!
lines.en: Mister, mister! Throw me some beads!

lines.kr: Li pe pa tenndé twa.
lines.en: He can’t hear you.

lines.kr: Misyé! Mo la!
lines.en: Mister! Here I am!

lines.kr: Li tro lwin astœr.
lines.en: He’s too far away now.

lines.kr: Fé tensyon, mô frær!
lines.en: Look out, brother!

lines.kr: Mé ki çé li garoshé apré twa?
lines.en: But what did he throw you?

lines.kr: Çé dê biy en vær!
lines.en: It’s some glass beads!

lines.kr: Mé m’olé ça osit!
lines.en: But I want some too!
